findings.problem: The same field uses two different terms. The TUI team editor labels a team's aliases «عرفی نام» (ur/tui.team_authoring.aliases, and aliases_hint «… خالی سے عرفی نام ہٹ جائیں گے»). A user who sets «عرفی نام» in /team edit then sees «متبادل نام» for the same values on the settings facts line. The translator anchored on cli.*.status_alias and browser reconcile («X کا متبادل»), which is a different concept: a command that stands in for another command, not a team's extra names.
findings.evidence: ur/tui.team_authoring.json: aliases='عرفی نام'; aliases_hint='کاما سے الگ نام · خالی سے عرفی نام ہٹ جائیں گے'. The glossary has no alias row. notes.md: 'alias | cli.*.status_alias / browser reconcile | … ur متبادل نام'.
findings.also: The glossary proposal in notes.md should give ur «عرفی نام» for the team/entity-alias sense; «متبادل» stays for the CLI sense 'alias of <command>'. With aliases 'ops, pod-a' the suggested value is 18 cells; the current value is 22.

tui.app.notes: member_count matches led_by and tui.small.network_panel.member_count byte-for-byte (رکن/اراکین); count 0 selects other and renders '0 اراکین', which reads naturally. Counts 0-100 render in at most 10 cells against maxCells 14; only 1000000 reaches 14 (en: 15). no_description matches tui.library.detail_no_description verbatim at 15/30 cells, and dropping projects' «ابھی» is correct because en has no 'yet'. fallback 'ٹیم' matches the glossary. The Latin ':' matches led_by «قیادت:». The catalogues already split the member plural: اراکین (led_by, community, network_panel) vs ارکان (team_authoring.members, wire.tool_rows). The translation follows its same-line sibling; this split does not gate, but a glossary row would settle it.

tui.projects.notes: «{shown} کردار» is the same in both arms, which is correct direct-case Urdu (کرداروں would be oblique). کردار matches TUI tui.authoring.role and wire.settings «بلٹ اِن کردار»; رول appears only in CLI help (cli.teams_help, cli.exec_help), so کردار is the right TUI choice. {manager} stays a Latin identifier in source order. Counts 0-100 render in 17-19 cells, the same as en; there is no maxCells. Bidi: no control characters. display.py wraps ur lines in RLI…PDI (not FSI, as the style guide says), so a leading LTR {manager} does not flip paragraph direction. No defect.
